title: QueryAudit
description: The query parameters of the administrative audit query, derived from identity_application::administration::QueryAudit. administrative_only is NOT optional and defaults to nothing: a caller that omits it gets the whole trail, and the flag is spelled out because the two are different questions.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; QueryAuditQuery has no body and no route serves it

user_id.description: Restrict to events ABOUT one user. `about`, not `by`: the actor filter is the separate actor_id field. AuditEventType::concerns_a_user is false for the three application events, which name an application rather than a person, so this filter legitimately returns nothing for those.

actor_id.description: Restrict to events BY one actor — the administrator who performed the action. Null in the row when no administrator acted.

since_ms.description: Only events at or after this time, in milliseconds since the epoch. A bound, not a window: 'since 1700000000000' is answerable, 'the last week' is not, because the latter depends on when you asked.

administrative_only.description: Only administrative events — those where an administrator changing an account caused them. Not nullable, so there is no reading of an absent value to get wrong. AuditEventType::is_administrative is the closed list: user_suspended, user_unsuspended, user_role_changed, all_sessions_revoked, application_registered, application_updated, application_secret_rotated.

x-accepted-values.constraining: a plain bool in Rust; the seven values are a property of the enum, not of this field

limit.description: Page size. Bounded by the repository.

offset.description: Page offset. Bounded by the repository.

x-response: QueryAuditOutcome — { events: AdminAuditRow[], has_more: boolean }, newest first. A console must NOT render an empty list as 'nothing happened': an empty audit log is a specific and alarming claim, and during the bootstrap phase events ARE being recorded server-side while only the query is deferred. Saying 'no events' when events exist and cannot be read is the worst thing an operator investigating an incident could be told.
x-metadata-is-already-redacted: AdminAuditRow.metadata is a BTreeMap<String, String> — a BTreeMap and not a HashMap because an audit row's JSON must serialise in a stable order to be diffable in a review. The values arrive redacted: redaction is the writer's job, and a console that trusted the trail to redact on read would be relying on a property the wire format does not carry.
